title: Assess and Halt on Quality Regression During Model Swaps
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Implement an automated evaluation-and-gate workflow that runs curated quality suites whenever a model version swap occurs in the catalog or when a customer pins a new model version. The system should compare key quality metrics to a baseline, surface results to the Console, and automatically pause rollouts / route-back to the previous version when regressions exceed configured thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: On any catalog model version change or customer-initiated pin, an eval job is automatically enqueued using the appropriate eval suite
Eval results computed within configured SLAs (default 10 minutes for small suites), with pass/fail decision recorded in the catalog and visible in Console
When threshold(s) for any critical metric are exceeded, rollout to the new version is paused and traffic remains on the previous model; an alert is raised to owners
Configurable thresholds per-model and per-customer; defaults provided for common regression types (semantic similarity, hallucination rate, safety flags, latency regression)
Audit trail recorded (who initiated pin, which eval suite was used, raw metrics, pass/fail decision, automated actions taken)
E2E tests that simulate a model swap and validate gating behavior are present in ci/eval-gate-tests
proposed_solution: Wire the model-catalog change events (both catalog-side publishes and customer pin calls) into the eval-runner. For catalog-wide model swaps use the central eval suite registry; for customer-pinned models prefer customer-scoped eval suites if present. Run evals in a sandbox cluster with controlled traffic replay or synthetic prompts. Compute metric diffs against the active pinned version baseline and apply a decision engine that enforces configurable thresholds and a rollback/pause automation path.
implementation_tasks: event: add catalog change and pin hooks that emit standardized payloads (catalog-service) - PR: github.com/redwood/catalog#PR-3892
runner: extend eval-runner to accept `swap-eval` jobs and a baseline reference id
suites: map models to default eval suites and add customer override path in the Console
decision-engine: implement comparator with threshold config and hysteresis to avoid flapping
playback infra: provide a secure, rate-limited traffic-replay queue for private and hosted contexts
console: UI to show live eval progress, diff visualizations, and one-click rollback
policy: audit log entry and alerting integration with PagerDuty/Slack
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): wire events and run evals for catalog model swaps only in staging clusters
Phase 2: enable eval gating for internal Redwood customers and test with a small set of partners
Phase 3: enable gating for all customer-pin flows with opt-out flag for low-risk customers
Phase 4: GA and toggle removal after 6 weeks of stable operation
test_plan: unit tests for comparator logic (thresholds, hysteresis)
integration test that simulates a catalog publish and validates eval job lifecycle
e2e: deploy new model version to canary cluster, run live eval with replayed traffic and assert pause on regression
load test: run 50 concurrent small suites to confirm eval-runner scaling and SLAs
security review of traffic-replay mechanism for PII/leakage risk
risks: Eval suites may not cover customer-specific prompts, causing false negatives/positives
Eval-runner capacity could become a bottleneck during large catalog rollouts
Traffic-replay in private deployments may be constrained by customer network policies
Aggressive thresholds could block safe upgrades; too lax thresholds may miss regressions
Audit/logging must be tamper-proof for compliance-sensitive customers
